newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES, COETZER ADVANCE, SANCHEZ VICARIO UPSET.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES, COETZER ADVANCE, SANCHEZ VICARIO UPSET.

text.p: Second seed Monica Seles survived and third seed Amanda Coetzer thrived to take their places in the quarter-finals of the Toshiba Tennis Classic.
But three-time finalist Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, who has struggled all year, was one of three seeded players bounced out of the tournament in the second round on Wednesday.

The third-ranked Seles slipped past Japan's Ai Sugiyama 6-4 6-4 in a sloppy match which featured 12 service breaks, while South African Coetzer needed just 66 minutes to pound out a 6-2 6-1 victory over Ann-Gaelle Sidot of France.

The fourth-seeded Sanchez, who in happier times earned the nickname "Barcelona bumble bee" for the way she buzzed around the court hitting winners, had little sting in her shots and was swatted out of the tournament by Sandrine Testud of France 6-1 6-2.
"Sandrine just played very consistently today," said the Spaniard. "She didn't miss a lot and I missed a few."
Testud, who took one hour and 28 minutes to oust Sanchez, insisted the score was misleading.
"It was a tough match, said the 20th-ranked Frenchwoman. "It was much closer than the final score."
Joining Sanchez on the sidelines was fifth seed Anke Huber of Germany and eighth seed Irina Spirlea of Romania.
Huber was upended by Yayuk Basuki of Indonesia 6-2 2-6 6-2, while Spirlea was crushed by Natasha Zvereva of Belarus 6-2 6-0.
In other second-round contests, sixth seed Mary Pierce bounced French Fed Cup teammate Nathalie Tauziat 6-2 6-1 and seventh-seeded Spaniard Conchita Martinez downed American Lisa Raymond 6-3 3-6 6-1.
In the late marquee matchup, world number one Martina Hingis of Switzerland takes her 50-1 1997 match record against rising American teenager Venus Williams.
Seles, who stumbled toward a possible final-round showdown with Hingis, is still searching for her best form.
"My game has not been there, the consistency," she said. "That's been the story of my year. I'm winning 6-3, 5-2 up and losing matches. I'm trying to improve upon that."

Seles prevailed with service breaks in the final game of each set against an error-prone Sugiyama. And even though she converted seven of nine break points, the former world number one lost her own serve five times.
"There were times where I got impatient," she said. "It was a very up and down game. I don't think I'm playing such great tennis.
"I feel I played good tennis for couple of games then defensive tennis for a couple of games. Ai gave me a lot of help," Seles admitted.
